title: LycheeMemory V2: Efficient Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents via Semantic Segment-Level Consolidation

visual_explainer.blocker: Per-paper GPT Image backfill is blocked in this run because two fresh isolated ReFind renders ignored their paper-specific brief and produced an unrelated dashboard with fabricated metadata. After repeated generator-level paper-identity failure, no ungrounded LycheeMemory V2 render was published.

analysis.tldr: LycheeMemory V2 makes consolidation granularity a first-class systems knob: batching semantically coherent exchanges into segments cuts high-frequency LLM construction calls, while semantic rather than fixed boundaries preserve enough event/temporal structure to improve accuracy instead of merely trading quality for cost.
analysis.problem: Eager per-turn LLM consolidation is expensive, but coarse summaries or mechanical batching can delete fine-grained evidence. Existing efficiency work often changes what is stored or how retrieval works without isolating how frequently and at what semantic granularity consolidation should run.
analysis.core_idea: Buffer exchanges online and finalize a segment using deterministic embedding-based surprise/cohesion signals. Invoke the LLM once per finalized semantic segment, normalize its output into typed self-contained records with bounded cross-segment reference context, index those records by entity/topic/time/event-frame relations, and use a query planner plus deterministic multi-route retrieval to assemble compact evidence.

memory_design.write: Accumulate exchanges until a semantic boundary or cap finalizes the active segment; perform one LLM encoding call for the whole segment instead of one call per turn, carrying limited same-session reference context only for disambiguation.
memory_design.organize: Normalize segment output into typed records with entities, topics, temporal scopes, provenance, and event-frame links; insert them into an append-only store with semantic and lightweight structured evidence indexes.
memory_design.read: A query planner creates typed recall routes over semantic records, entity/topic/temporal/event-frame indexes, and raw turns; deterministic modules retrieve, rerank, fuse, and diversity-select a compact evidence context.
memory_design.update_forget: The store is append-only in this work. Segment finalization controls when consolidation happens, but explicit contradiction repair, deletion, and long-term forgetting are not central mechanisms.

compared_to: Eager per-turn consolidation with the same overall framework
Fixed-window batching that preserves batching but removes semantic boundary detection
A-Mem, Mem0, TiMem, MemoryOS, and other conversational-memory baselines under GPT-4.1-Mini
analysis.evidence: On LoCoMo with GPT-4.1-Mini, full LycheeMemory reaches 89.22 accuracy with 204.1K construction tokens. Eager consolidation uses 849.9K tokens (+316%) yet falls to 81.88; fixed-window batching uses slightly fewer tokens (174.7K) but falls to 82.40, isolating batching as the cost saver and semantic boundaries as the accuracy-preserving factor. Relative to A-Mem, construction tokens fall 86.0% on LoCoMo and 75.9% on LongMemEval-S; query tokens are also lower. Representation and retrieval ablations are substantial: summary-level records score 80.78, record-vector-only retrieval 81.75, and removing fusion/rerank/diversity drops to 66.62 versus 89.22 full.
analysis.why_it_matters: The paper adds an orthogonal design axis to memory efficiency: not only what to remember or how to retrieve it, but the temporal/semantic granularity at which expensive memory transformation runs. A memory pipeline can save construction cost without collapsing into coarse summaries if it batches around coherent event boundaries.
limitations: Evaluation is text-only conversational memory on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S; multimodal memory, acting agents, online feedback, and production deployment are not covered.
The paper optimizes token cost, not end-to-end database latency, index storage, cache behavior, or monitoring overhead.
Preference-heavy questions remain a weakness relative to systems with dedicated persona/profile modeling.
Semantic boundary quality depends on the embedding/scoring pipeline and the chosen threshold; transfer across domains and conversation styles is not established.
